chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa al-Ashari narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khasa'i, from Durays al-Kinasi, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli in a tradition of his which we have condensed

He said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to name the Qaim so that I may recognize him by his name. He said: O Abu Khalid! You have asked me about a matter, if the children of Fatimah had known it, they would have desired to cut him into pieces.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim, title of the Mahdi
key_terms.بَنِي فَاطِمَةَ: Children of Fatimah, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ضَعْفَةً ضَعْفَةً: Into pieces, indicating intense desire or secrecy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the secrecy of the Qaim's name?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the doctrine of *al-Kafāʾ* (sufficiency) and the strategic concealment of the Imam's name to prevent premature identification or political usurpation by rivals. The Imam’s hyperbolic response underscores the preciousness of this knowledge, suggesting that even the Ahl al-Bayt would have eagerly guarded it if it were not divinely ordained to remain hidden until the appointed time.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 278 - Ahmad bin Muhammad Isa Ashari has narrated from Muhammad bin Sinan from Muhammad bin Yahya Khathami from Zaris Kinasi from Abu Khalid Kabuli in the tradition, which we have condensed:

I asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) to pronounce the name of the Qaim, so that I may recognize him through his name. The Imam said: Aba Khalid, you have asked about a thing and about one such that even if his children had recognized him, they would also have become jealous and have cut him into pieces.
